summary: Daily public transport usage has rebounded to pre‑pandemic levels, while fuel savings remain substantial at 35.7 million litres per week. However, low fuel prices and uneven work‑from‑home adoption keep overall mobility high, posing economic and equity challenges.

signals.detail: Weekly fuel savings of 35.7 M litres represent 42 % of the MCO peak, indicating continued environmental benefit. The magnitude has slipped from the peak, suggesting a gradual return to higher fuel consumption as mobility recovers.

Daily PT trips reached 1.49 million, slightly above the pre‑pandemic daily average (~1.43 million). The ridership component of the MF‑Index is at full score, confirming a strong modal shift back to public transport.

High mobility scores in Retail & Services, Logistics and Construction (85‑95) signal elevated travel‑related costs and congestion risk. These sectors contribute disproportionately to economic exposure as WFH adoption remains low.

WFH adoption is uneven: 60 % in Public & GLCs versus only 15 % in Retail & Services, creating a disparity in exposure to fuel price shocks and congestion. Equity‑focused policies are needed to balance benefits across sectors.
The MF‑Index sits at 54, reflecting only moderate progress toward a sustainable mobility mix. Ultra‑low fuel prices (RM0.05/L) undermine incentives for a lasting shift to low‑carbon modes.

recommendation: Introduce a modest fuel excise (e.g., RM0.10 per litre) to restore price signals, while expanding EV charging infrastructure and subsidising PT fare discounts for high‑mobility sectors. Set a target to raise the overall MF‑Index to 65 by end‑2027 through sector‑specific WFH incentives and a 10 % increase in PT ridership capacity.
